title: Quickstart usability + microcopy runbook: standup notes
content:
Standup: Quickstart usability + microcopy experiments (lightning runbook)
Date: 2026-09-02
Facilitator: Aisha K.
Attendees: Aisha Kapoor, Tom Lee, Diego Alvarez, Maya Chen, optionally UX researcher Priyanka Rao sat in for 20m
Objective: Triage last week's pilot with 12 external developers, decide which microcopy variants to A/B in the public beta quickstart, and assign follow-ups for SDK/CLI patches and dashboard copy updates.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Pilot summary: 12 developers (mix of startup and in-house platform engineers) ran the JS quickstart + Python example. Median time-to-first-successful-request was 9m (target 7m). Top friction points: ambiguous error text when API key not found, confusing default model chooser in CLI, and missing example for streaming with tool-calls.
- Microcopy experiments: We have 3 high-confidence changes for the quickstart README/CLI prompts and 2 medium-risk dashboard CTA variants. Decide to A/B test microcopy A vs B for the CLI key prompt and publish microcopy C (informational) in README.
- Immediate actions: Patch CLI to make API key error actionable; merge SDK PR #812; schedule dashboard copy push for Sep 8.

Notes / Observations from pilot runs:
- Time-to-first-success: median 9m, IQR 6m-15m. Outliers (30m+) were due to 1) corporate network blocking outbound on 443 (note in doc), 2) user using python v2.7 environment.
- Top three explicit comments from participants:
  1) "Error message doesn't help me know where to put the key" (saw it 7 times)
  2) "CLI assumes npm install global; please show npx alternative" (5 times)
  3) "Streaming example in README uses server-side code only; want a small client-side snippet" (4 times)
- Implicit friction: participants who scanned README before running missed the step to set REDWOOD_REGION; we need an inline verification step in CLI (suggestion: detect missing region and confirm).

Microcopy variants included in this doc (raw):
- CLI API key error (A): \"No API key found. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment or run \`redwood login\` to store it locally.\"
- CLI API key error (B): \"We couldn't find a Redwood API key — either add REDWOOD_API_KEY to your environment (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...) or run \`redwood login\` to authenticate.\"
- README quickstart header (C): \"Get a hello-world response from Redwood in under 5 minutes — copy-paste the example below and replace YOUR_API_KEY.\"
- Dashboard CTA (1): \"Try with your own API key — quickstart in the Console\"
- Dashboard CTA (2): \"Launch sample app with demo credentials (no risk)\"

Decisions from the meeting:
- Use microcopy B for CLI API key error (more explicit instructions). Rationale: higher clarity from pilot quotes. Owner: Tom L. (implement in CLI repo).
- Publish README header copy C immediately. Owner: Maya C. (docs repo PR).
- Dashboard CTA: we'll A/B test CTA 1 vs CTA 2 for two weeks with 50/50 split, measure click-through and time-to-first-request. Owner: Diego A. (analytics + console).
- Merge SDK PR #812 (contains better streaming example and updated error handling). Owner: Aisha K. to unblock CI.

Action items (who / what / deadline):
- Tom Lee: implement explicit API-key check + improved error B in CLI (PR branch: fix/cli-apikey-check). Due: 2026-09-07. Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/812 (follow-up).
- Maya Chen: submit docs PR for README header + add npx example in quickstart. Due: 2026-09-05. Draft: docusaurus/docs/quickstarts/quickstart-js.md (work in progress).
- Diego Alvarez: wire A/B split in Console experiment framework, add metrics (CTR, time-to-first-request, signup drop-off). Due: 2026-09-08. Jira: ENG-4721.
- Priyanka Rao (UX): prepare test script for 6 additional external devs focusing on streaming + tool-calls; recruit via partner Slack. Due: 2026-09-10.
- Aisha Kapoor: unblock CI failure for SDK PR, coordinate release notes. Due: 2026-09-04.

Blockers / Risks:
- Analytics: Console experiment framework currently lacks time-to-first-request as a surfaced metric. Diego flagged need for backend event to be instrumented. Risk: can't evaluate effect size quickly.
- Release windows: Console copy push scheduled alongside infra maintenance on Sep 8 — coordinate with SRE.
- Legal: demo credentials CTA (dashboard CTA 2) flagged by legal for rate-limiting and data retention terms. Need quick consult.

Quick patches and snippets (dev notes):
- Suggested CLI pseudocode for API key check:
  if (!env.REDWOOD_API_KEY) {
    print(\"No API key found. Run \`redwood login\` or set REDWOOD_API_KEY=... to continue. See docs: <<link>>\");
    exit(1);
  }
- README npx alternatives: show both \`npm i -g @redwood/sdk\` and \`npx @redwood/sdk quickstart\` with short note: \"npx runs without global install\".
- Streaming example: include both Node fetch + SSE client snippet and Python aiohttp streaming client small examples (3 lines each) — keep them minimal.

Testing plan for microcopy A/B:
- Metric: time-to-first-successful-request, successful-request rate in 30 minutes, CTA CTR. Secondary: user reported clarity in post-task survey (Likert scale).
- N size: start with 1k quickstart impressions or 14 days whichever comes first; pilot will run initially with partner devs (n=18) then open to public.
- Safety: do not expose real customer data in demo flow; demo tokens must be rate-limited and flagged.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should quickstart recommend quantized model variants for cost-sensitive demos? (parking: talk to Applied ML)
- Where to put the streaming client snippet in the doc hierarchy to avoid duplication? (docs owner: Maya)
- Can we add a tiny verification step in the Console that alerts if region not set? (discuss with Console team)

Notes to self / informal bits:
- Quick fix wins: README header + npx snippet + CLI API key error probably will reduce median time by ~1.5–2m based on heuristic from pilot transcripts.
- Keep microcopy options short and direct; pilots show devs ignore long paragraphs.
- Remember to update changelog for SDK release (small note under "What's changed").

Next standup / checkpoint:
- Quick async check-in: Sep 05 in #devexp-quickstarts channel — short status pins from owners.
- Follow-up meeting to review A/B metrics: Sep 16 (two-week cadence for CTA experiment).

Appendix: pilot raw quotes (selected)
- "I set the key but CLI still complained — turned out I set the wrong env name (API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY)"
- "I prefer a copy that tells me exactly how to run a stream; the current example feels server-heavy"
- "Npx examples are lifesavers for quick tryouts"

Draft checklist for merge/ship (to paste in PR):
- [ ] CLI: api-key check implemented and unit-tested
- [ ] SDK: fix streaming example included, CI green
- [ ] Docs: README header + npx snippet + streaming client snippet merged
- [ ] Console: CTA A/B flags created, analytics instrumented for time-to-first-request
- [ ] Legal: sign-off for demo credentials flow (if CTA 2 used)

End of notes.

-- Aisha K.
